name: Flood Fill
description: An algorithm that determines and alters the area connected to a given node in a multi-dimensional array. It functions similarly to the 'bucket fill' paint tool, traversing adjacent matching cells recursively.

code.python:
def floodFill(image, sr, sc, newColor):
    color = image[sr][sc]
    if color == newColor: return image
    R, C = len(image), len(image[0])
    def dfs(r, c):
        if r < 0 or r >= R or c < 0 or c >= C or image[r][c] != color: return
        image[r][c] = newColor
        dfs(r+1, c); dfs(r-1, c); dfs(r, c+1); dfs(r, c-1)
    dfs(sr, sc)
    return image

name: Greedy Strategy
description: An algorithmic paradigm that makes the locally optimal choice at each stage in the hope of finding a global optimum. Greedy strategies require two key properties: Greedy Choice Property and Optimal Substructure.

code.python:
def minCoinsGreedy(coins, amount):
    coins.sort(reverse=True)
    count = 0
    for coin in coins:
        count += amount // coin
        amount %= coin
    return count if amount == 0 else -1

name: Memoization (Top-Down DP)
description: An optimization technique that speeds up recursive algorithms by caching the results of expensive subproblem calls. When a subproblem is encountered again, the cached result is returned directly.

code.python:
def fibMemo(n, memo={}):
    if n <= 1: return n
    if n in memo: return memo[n]
    memo[n] = fibMemo(n - 1, memo) + fibMemo(n - 2, memo)
    return memo[n]

name: Tabulation (Bottom-Up DP)
description: An iterative approach to dynamic programming. It starts by solving the base cases and fills a table (array/matrix) sequentially from the bottom up, ensuring that all subproblems are solved before their results are needed.

code.python:
def fibTab(n):
    if n <= 1: return n
    dp = [0] * (n + 1)
    dp[1] = 1
    for i in range(2, n + 1): dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2]
    return dp[n]
